## Summary

Built a complete Angular 19 standalone CRUD demo at `/private/tmp/dsb-eval/sonnet-5/A-2/blueprint-crud` per the spec: login (hardcoded `admin`/`admin`, guards both ways), an authenticated shell (header with leftward-opening profile menu, footer with link columns), an 8-tile dashboard (custom bar chart, live-updating log viewer), and a full `/users` CRUD table with all four modals (delete confirm, read-only details, edit, invite) wired to `angular-in-memory-web-api`.

Since this is the "no infrastructure" arm, I pulled real values from the Figma file (via a subagent, since the raw payload was too large for direct reading) and consolidated them into one `:root` CSS custom-property system in `styles.scss` (colors, spacing, radii, type scale) plus global atomic classes (`.btn`, `.badge`, `.field`, `.card`), so every component draws from a single source instead of scattering literals — directly addressing the stated failure mode for this arm.

I verified the build and the running app with Playwright (no local `chromium-cli`, so I installed `playwright` + Chromium in a temp dir): login validation, dashboard, profile menu, users table, and all four dialogs render correctly, and a full create → edit → delete round-trip against the in-memory API works with zero console errors. One real bug surfaced and was fixed during this: wrapping the edit/invite form body and footer in a shared `<ng-container [formGroup]>` silently dropped all projected content, since Angular's content-projection `select` doesn't recurse into `ng-container`'s children when picking a slot — moved `[formGroup]` onto the `modal-body` div directly instead.

**Unverified / invented (flagged per instructions):** the header's nav labels ("Dashboard"/"Team Members"), the footer's link columns and legal links (S0 required them but the fetched Figma frame only showed a minimal footer), and the dashboard's two-column responsive breakpoints (no mobile frame existed in the fetched Figma data).
